name: dhcp-c308df0f-blind29-ots
instr:
# dhcp-regen

A Go program uses this library to ask for automatically assigned network addresses and boot settings, to answer such requests, and to make sense of what comes back, over both the older four-byte address family and the newer sixteen-byte one. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the calling programs changed, yet exchanges that used to be handled correctly now come back wrong: values vanish when read back, wire data decodes to the wrong numbers or is waved through where it should be refused and refused where it should be accepted, and several everyday operations now fail outright. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits.

Take first the act of putting a request together and reading back what was just put into it. Build an inquiry aimed at a particular host, attach while building it the address of the machine that ought to answer, then ask the finished inquiry for that address: nothing comes back, as though it had never been attached, and every field whose value is a single four-byte address behaves the same way. Ask that a host wait three hundred seconds before preferring a network offering only the newer address family, read that back, and the duration is zero rather than five minutes. Attaching a free-text label for the kind of equipment doing the asking writes the two permitted encodings the wrong way round: request the standardised form, in which each item is preceded by its own length, and the plain text with no length count
